title: Slow On the Ramp
hook: The exit is named. The highway is still fast.
scene: Daylight rain, afternoon, I-5 south. A green exit panel sits far enough ahead that you can still choose. The right lane will become the ramp. Your cluster is highway speed. The curve on the ramp is tight. Dumping speed here, on the travel lanes, turns the stack behind you into a wall of lamps. The ramp is where the number dies.
decision: You have the exit. Where does the speed come off?

options.text: Brake now in the travel lane so you arrive at the ramp already slow
options.result: You dump speed on I-5. The box behind you stands on it. You made a highway stop for a ramp that still had its own pavement.

options.text: Hold highway speed past the gore and brake in the middle of the curve
options.result: You enter the bend still hot. The rear of the box steps out. Yaw on a wet ramp is how a schedule ends.

options.text: Skip this exit and take the next one so you do not have to slow at all
options.result: You miss a named exit because slowing felt rude. The schedule just grew a loop. The ramp was the legal place to lose the number.

options.text: Hold speed on the highway, signal early, drop the number on the ramp
options.result: You keep their speed until the ramp owns you. The stalk talked four to six seconds back. On the ramp you tap the brakes and the curve gets the posted number.

debrief: Pick the exit early. Do not slow on the highway. Hold highway speed until the ramp owns you.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part one
source.teaching_target: Identify the exit early; do not slow on the highway; signal 4–6 seconds before the ramp.
